_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.holes is what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hit for N
entries.codex:
Shield takes it first, then Armour reduces it.
Barrier, Brittle and hit effects apply.

design.holes: The three ways damage lands, the standard's rule 39 (Ryan, 24 November: "I like hit for N, suffer N damage, and lose N hull as the format examples that we want"), given a heading of their own in the keywords list on his yes of 25 November to a Damage section in place of reminders on each tip. Listed, never matched in a line (Terms.UNMATCHED): "Hit" is a label's word. The text is a session's draft.

entries.name: Suffer N damage
entries.codex:
Not a hit. Shield takes it first.
Armour, Barrier, Brittle and hit effects do not apply.

design.holes: The three ways damage lands, the standard's rule 39 (Ryan, 24 November: "I like hit for N, suffer N damage, and lose N hull as the format examples that we want"), given a heading of their own in the keywords list on his yes of 25 November to a Damage section in place of reminders on each tip. Listed, never matched in a line (Terms.UNMATCHED): "Hit" is a label's word. The text is a session's draft.

entries.name: Lose N
entries.codex:
Comes straight off the Hull, HP or Shield named.
Nothing reduces or adds to it.

design.holes: The three ways damage lands, the standard's rule 39 (Ryan, 24 November: "I like hit for N, suffer N damage, and lose N hull as the format examples that we want"), given a heading of their own in the keywords list on his yes of 25 November to a Damage section in place of reminders on each tip. Listed, never matched in a line (Terms.UNMATCHED): "Hit" is a label's word. The text is a session's draft.

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the machine is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: HP
entries.codex: A foe's health. What gets past its armour takes HP off, and at zero the foe falls. A machine's health is its hull.

design.holes: A machine's health is its hull; the engine's code may say either word.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage hits shield before hull. A shield absorbs its number: a blow costs it its damage, and whatever it cannot absorb passes to the hull, armour coming off it there. Nothing mends a shield by itself: a reboot brings it back whole, and a component, a module or a passive may add to one that still stands, up to the chassis maximum. A shield at nothing is Broken, and takes none until its machine reboots. The shield is full as every fight opens, as the heat starts at zero; nothing returns on the map.

design.holes: Shield sizes are placeholders. No chassis regenerates: the reboot refills a shield, and a passive, a module or a status may grant a regen.

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: A component that prints heat adds it when spent, and it stays: nothing cools a machine by itself. Heat may pass the chassis maximum, and what stands past it is Overheated: at the end of your turn, before the enemy acts, it burns hull one for one, every turn it stands there, and the first such turn since the machine's last reboot breaks its shield. A reboot takes the heat to nothing; a vent, a module or a passive that cools takes some off, what stands past the maximum first. A machine the burn wrecks is lost on its own turn. Foes never add heat: a Scorched machine's weapons and equipment aimed at foes run hotter for the turn.

design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow. No chassis cools: the reboot vents, and a cooling a piece grants must stay below a typical weapon's heat or heat never matters (tuning).

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Two rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent die. A reroll lands on any other component on the die, never the one showing; a second copy of the same component may come up. Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds, unless a Giant Petrel fights: its Maverick's Playbook banks up to three left unspent as your turn ends, for the next round.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase, never inside a fight. It fills at the ramp's beat (3 turns, 2 from Convergence 8), a turn short of its peak as a battle opens, and the beat halves once at the Rupture. When full it resets and peaks: the rift and every tear open before the peak each send 2 packs, a hunting pack comes out of the rift every second peak, and new tears open, each peak's nearer the wall. It never stops: the boss's seal breaking does not quiet it.

design.holes: The interval step inside a battle (the escalation a stall would meet) is on the ramp's table at zero until the turtle read asks for it.

entries.name: Rupture meter
entries.codex: Fills by the menace of the packs you kill, in any fight however it ends, toward the tier's Fractures (three, four or five), each later one costing more. The last, the Rupture, takes the packs the field opens with and the rift's first two peaks send, one lone patrol left over, and 4 more for each elite the tier's Fractures bring. The Rupture breaks the boss's seal, and nothing else does: a cleared field is breathing room until the next peak.

design.holes: Shown as a bar under the gate's with a notch a Fracture, a first cut; the beats, the patrol left and the steps are placeholders.

entries.name: Fracture
entries.codex: A step of the Rupture meter, paid out as a fight ends. At the Fractures the tier names (tier one's first; tier two's first and third; tier three's first, second and fourth) an elite emerges at the rift, the lead domain's elites in turn and never twice in a battle. The last Fracture is the Rupture.

design.holes: The prize a Fracture may bring is not built (decided after the meter is played).

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: Each pusher makes for the stretch of the wall its threat rating sends it to: the ends for 1, the middle for 3, between them for 2. A pusher that ends its walk beside any hex of the gate or the wall strikes the gate's bar every turn: 5 for each Frame it is a fight for, less as it loses Sprites, at least 1. The whole wall is the target, so no line plugs it. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.holes: The gate damage formula is a placeholder; city defences along the wall are not built.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.codex: A component that deals damage. Used on a Sprite within reach: deals its damage, then its keywords apply.

design.holes: The engine's kind is attack for a weapon and a debuff alike: a debuff is an attack of no damage (Face.is_debuff), so code asks is_weapon() for this word and is_attack() for both.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.codex: A component that deals no damage: a buff used on a Frame, or a debuff used on a Sprite within reach.

entries.name: Buff component
entries.codex: Equipment used on a Frame. Applies the status and stacks shown on the die.

entries.name: Direct
entries.codex: Targets front-rank Sprites, back-rank Sprites with nothing in front, and Exposed Sprites.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any Sprite.

entries.name: Spread
entries.codex: Also hits all Sprites beside the target, dealing {N} damage.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (cleave), and the validator asks for it on a weapon. The half it dealt from 26 October retired 28 October (Ryan): at single digits a neighbour's half killed no rank and file. A piece may carry it beside Penetrate, the plus round its target; Splash, the two under one word, was cut on 15 November (Ryan: "It might be a more interesting game with only the other area shapes, with a few select pieces carrying both spread and penetrate together").

entries.name: Penetrate
entries.codex: Also hits all other Sprites in the same column, dealing {N} damage.

design.holes: Its number rides on the entry beside the keyword (penetrate), and the validator asks for it on a weapon.

entries.name: Every Sprite
entries.codex: Hits every Sprite for full damage. No hit is Targeted.

design.holes: A keyword from 2 November (Ryan: 'Every foe is a targeting mode, just like spread, penetrate, and splash, it should be listed as such and given a keyword'), a targeting mode in its own right since 4 November ('Silence should not narrow targeting modes, that's why I'm switching them to targeting modes'), drawn in the die's targeting slot. A working name, the foes' Every Machine mirrored. A weapon's too since 12 November, when Sweep went (Ryan: the Whip Scorpion's and the Musk Ox's specials "a 'target all'"): it strikes every foe for its whole number and none is its one target (Ryan, 12 November: "Target all shouldn't need a target in the same way that sweep didn't. Why would only the first target pop shock? That's weird and useless"), so a Shock is doubled and spent on each and, with no primary target, no Ricochet follows it. No area keyword rides it.

entries.name: Every Frame
entries.codex: Applies to every Frame, including this one.

design.holes: Every Foe's mirror on the team's side (2 November; a targeting mode since 4 November); a working name. Its mark is the three hexes under a low arch, its own cell lit (Ryan, 4 November: 'the difference is whether the center one is lit or not, its two modes, even if the every ally doesn't actually exist in game, yet'): no piece carries it yet. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Every Other Frame
entries.codex: Applies to every Frame except this one.

design.holes: Every Ally's other mode (4 November), the Mooring Screens' team shield; a working name. Its mark is Every Ally's with its own cell dark. Never a vent's (the validator).

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Cryo per hit to each Sprite hit.

design.holes: Other pieces may lay it (marked for reuse as a healthier ally cooling than a vent). A rider on the mark is benched until the roster has room. The cooling a stack is a placeholder.

entries.name: Ablate
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Ablate per hit to each unit hit.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (ablate), and the validator asks for it. Burn until 15 November: the word is Ryan's, for an eroding that is not only fire ("Ablating or ablate is very clinical, it fits the military notation, and evokes eating though armour to me"). A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Lure
entries.codex: Hit: Change intended target to this Frame.

design.holes: No status and no chip: the arrow is the record. A draw by an ally is parked (the bible's redirection row).

entries.name: Shock
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply Shocked to each Sprite hit.

entries.name: Expose
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply 2 Exposed to each unit hit.

design.holes: The formation word exposed stays rules text, so the status's id is exposure. The foes' half is Ryan's of 15 November (the vocabulary pass's fourth and fifth rounds), built 16 November: a tier-two foe's at the least, the validator refusing it on anything dealt at tier one ("only in formations that feel thematic and fair, so that the player has tools to answer by that point"), and one out at a time ("Enemy units should be smart enough to only try to Expose one player unit at a time"). Its carriers since 17 November: the Goblin Warchief, the Basilisk, the Alpha Warg, the Lich and the Rider of the Wild Hunt, each a move of its own, and the Piercing Eye, whose Gaze carries it as a rider. A blow's Expose lays nothing while a machine stands Exposed, so a foe whose one move it is marks every other round at the most. The foes' text is a session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Disrupt
entries.codex: Resolve: Sprites hit switch to the next move they can use, keeping their target.

design.holes: Deterministic: the next move in the foe's list that its conditions allow, so a boss steps through its pattern.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply Suppressed to each Sprite hit.

entries.name: Swap
entries.codex:
Second target: another Sprite or an empty slot.
Resolve: The target and the second target swap places. Massive Sprites cannot move.

design.holes: A keyword until 15 November (Ryan: "Can be unique text, not a keyworded rider"): the piece's own rule, `swaps` on its entry, its mark kept on the die.

entries.name: Brittle
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Brittle per hit to each unit hit.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (brittle), and the validator asks for it. Flak on our side and Crush on the foes' until 15 November, one word on both since (Ryan: "Crushed and flak - agreed, brittle"). The word names the state, so a piece that lays it reads Brittle 2 and the Flak pieces keep their names; a verb for it is his to pick if he wants one. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Sap
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Sapped per hit to each Sprite hit.

design.holes: The keyword that lays Ryan's Sapped (11 November), first on the Baboon's Redshift Emitter.

entries.name: Juggernaut Drive
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Ignores Armour.
  Resolve: Consumed.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "After gaining Barrier, its next weapon attack gains Breach. The next attack breach will need to be represented by a purgeable buff, I'd just call it 'Juggernaut Breach.'" 15 November, Breach cut on our side: 'Change to explicit "ignores armour."', so the state shows under the passive's own name and the word Breach is gone from the game.

table.lasts: Until its next weapon attack

entries.name: Numbed
entries.codex:
When Suppressed would be applied: Prevent it and reduce stacks by 1.
Turn End: Reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: Ryan's clock (2 November): the chip reads as the rounds until it can be stunned again, so the stacks land after the decay phase; a stun lock costs its resist and one every round, so an all-in stun team can brute-force a boss at a price, and a Purge is the other key. The resist numbers are placeholders (content's resist; the bosses' by hand).

table.stacks: Yes: its stun resist as it recovers from a stun
table.lasts: A stack goes as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Paradox
entries.codex:
When another Debuff is applied: Gain 1 stack per stack applied.
At 5 or more stacks: Reduce stacks to 0 and gain Suppressed.

design.holes: The count is a placeholder (Ryan, 11 November: "we have no idea how many paradox stacks is balanced, we just decided on 3 or whatever as a placeholder without knowing how much status chips were going to get thrown around in the game as a whole"); a stack a debuff stack since that day, at five.

table.stacks: Yes: one for every debuff stack gained; at five or more it Suppresses and clears
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Volatile
entries.codex: Commit: Lose {N} Hull.

design.holes: Hull outright, where the Corrupted bite takes shield first. The number is a placeholder. A keyword with a chip until 26 October; a cost like heat since, so the die says the price and no chip does.

entries.name: Shield cost
entries.codex:
Commit: Lose {N} Shield.
Cannot be used without enough Shield.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 26 October: a price paid in the buffer, which overshield cheats out at the cost of two actions for one effect; the first entry with a condition on its play, so advanced pieces may follow.
design.holes: No piece carries it yet; the numbers are content's.

entries.name: Targets
entries.codex: Which Frames this can be used on, shown as three hexes under its mark: the middle is this Frame, the sides are the other Frames. A filled hex can be chosen.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: Resolve: All Sprites with Shock lose {N} HP.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November, his text: "I want to change Chain. The under-armour ping is simpler. Resolve: All Sprites with Shock, Static, or Sonic Needle lose {N} HP." Static is the debuff of his Static machine of 4 November, not yet built (docs/briefs/aphelion_static.md), so only Shock and Sonic Needle conduct until it lands. His words, not yet signed on the Text tab; 25 November, of the conductors: "the only non-exclusive conductor is Shock. So it's possible that we just need to mention Shock specifically", so Sonic Needle's and Static's own tips say they conduct it.

entries.name: Rapid
entries.codex: Resolve: Reroll this die for free, never onto this entry. This entry goes dark for the rest of the round.

design.holes: Its limiter is its own switch-off, the entry dark for the rest of the round (Ryan, 12 November: "rapid gets its innate cooldown zero back without the explicit display"), which no cleanse lifts; a Rapid vent is never below tier three and a Rapid shield never below tier two (the bible's Rapid row).

entries.name: Instant
entries.codex: Resolve: Reroll this die for free. May land on this entry again.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "the rapid no cooldown pieces change to a new keyword: Instant (reroll after use, can land on itself)". Every Instant piece carries a limiter, which the validator holds content to: a cooldown, heat, Volatile or a shield cost, or the store a charged form spends; a piece locked on a stepping die has the cylinder's odds (the Spin-Up's), and a piece Instant only while its machine rages has its heat (the Nemesis's Knuckles of Fury). An entry is Rapid or Instant, never both.

entries.name: Jam
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply Jammed to the entry shown by each Frame hit.

design.holes: Disable until 15 November (Ryan: "Rename to Jammed"); the rider follows the pattern, Jam lays Jammed.

entries.name: Destroy
entries.codex: After Hit: If Hull damage was dealt, destroy the entry the target's die shows.

design.holes: No foe carries it (Ryan, 15 November: "This can be a boss-level rider, that destroys the visible face if it damages hull at all. Only promoted form or superboss-level so we're not tuning the economy around it. No longer a general rule"). Its carrier is the foes' pass's, and the fight bot prices no entry's loss until one does.

entries.name: Immune
entries.codex: Immune to the effect named on the chip.

design.holes: Ryan, 15 November: "not as a blanket for all bosses, but for ones who need it for their fight to actually do something." Content: immune on a foe, suppress or disrupt, each true or the id of a move of its own that gathers. Three carriers since 17 November, on his yes to the bench's rows: the Pilgrim, Suppress, whose dread is that it keeps coming; the Obsidian Tyrant, Disrupt while Firestorm gathers, and the Ruby Colossus, Disrupt while Ultima gathers, whose rounds of warning are the fight. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Drain
entries.codex: After Hit: Heal HP equal to the Hull damage dealt.

design.holes: The Vampire Lord's (30 October), its bite and, below half, a drain at every machine. The genre's word (Drain), and the soft counter section 2 asks for: Ablating never stops healing. The hull alone, so the shield answers it: a drain of shield and hull walled the slowest trio at every HP tried, the shield, its answer to every blow, doing nothing against the heal. A rider on its blows until 16 November, and the unit's own Ability since, on Ryan's mark of 15 November ("This should be moved to an ability on the unit since it's on every attack. Like the Nob"): a chip on the foe, every blow of its, and no word on the blow. The text is a session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Timid
entries.codex: Attacks only while carrying a Buff, or with a Buff announced for it.

design.holes: Ryan, 20 November: "goblins only attack when they have any buff, or are predicted to get one" and "If a goblin is getting a shield from its peer in the intent, it should queue an attack". The foes announce in the order they strike, so a goblin reads the moves already out ahead of it, never one after it. The name is his (20 November: "Rename Safety in Numbers to Timid"); the text a session's draft.

entries.name: Corrupt
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Corrupted per hit to the entry shown by each Frame hit.

entries.name: Swallow
entries.codex:
Round End: Apply {N} Swallowed to the target.
Cannot target the last Frame able to act.

design.holes: Floraison's (30 October). The rounds, 1 to 3, are the move's, and no damage lands on the machine while it is held. The early release (31 October, Ryan agreeing Claude's lean): a quarter of the swallower's HP lost since the swallow, Clair Obscur's stagger in its smallest form, a round of the team's focus; the swallower loses nothing else, since a lost action on top would be a stun. A machine let go in the player's turn acts that round.

entries.name: Golden Rage
entries.codex:
Turn End: Gain {N} Golden.
Only usable while not Golden.

design.holes: The Thunder Ape's (4 November); see Golden. Its weight is content's, 2 so it comes about a round in three while calm.

entries.name: Merge
entries.codex:
Absorbs every other Sprite of the named kinds, healing the HP they had left, up to Max HP.
Gain {N} Empowered per Sprite absorbed.

design.holes: The King Gel's (30 October): every Gel, Bubble Gel, Metal Gel and half on the field. Content: effect merge, foe (an id or a list), value (the lift a foe taken in). A foe taken in leaves no last act and no split and is no kill of the team's; its pack's tally still counts it gone. It needs its kinds beside it, so the King Gel's escort is its own (an escort that names its boss).

entries.name: Purge
entries.codex: Resolve: Reduce stacks of every Buff on each unit hit by {N}.

design.holes: One id, dispel, on both sides (28 October); numbered 2 November (Ryan: "lower everything by N and price accordingly", a softer answer to armour and damage stacking that prices cheap and common; the Null Field Emitter at Purge 2, a placeholder). One purge on either side (Effects.purge): N stacks off every buff, whatever granted it (Ryan, 8 November: "A stack is a stack, doesn't matter where it came from"); retired with it the purge by source of 28 October (a die entry's stacks gone for good, a store's, a form's or a passive's put to sleep until the player's turn), which he called cryptic. What the unit is, its form or its passive mechanic, is an Ability and no buff, so no purge reaches it (the same day).

entries.name: Cleanse
entries.codex: Resolve: Remove every Debuff from the target, except those that cannot be cleansed.

design.holes: A Sprite's Cleanse lifts Suppressed too since 26 November (Ryan: "Change the cleanse to remove suppress, I never approved that"), so its line says no more than a Frame's. Cleanse and Purge stay two effects (his the same day: "Keep cleanse and purge seperate, I was confused").

entries.name: Shocked
entries.codex:
Hit By Weapon: If targeted, consume to double damage received, before applying defensive effects.
Conducts Chain.

table.lasts: Until the next team blow of a weapon

entries.name: Pinned
entries.codex:
When Brittle would be reduced: Consumed to prevent it.
Turn End: If there is no Brittle, removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "The Flak pin should be its own status that gets applied for one turn. I assume we're going to want a similar one for burning as well." Pinned Flak until 15 November, and what it holds Brittle since; the name is his ("Just \"Pinned.\"").

table.stacks: Never: a second pin refreshes it
table.lasts: Until the halving it stops

entries.name: Seared
entries.codex:
When Ablate would be reduced: Consumed to prevent it.
Turn End: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: coded in beside Brittle's pin, "since the Mastema will want it as a fitted piece, if nothing else". No piece lays it yet. The name is his, 15 November: "Rename 'Seared.'"

table.stacks: Never: a second pin refreshes it
table.lasts: Until the fade it stops

entries.name: Sapped
entries.codex:
Attacks Gain:
  Hit: -1 damage dealt per stack ({N}).
Turn End: Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: Ryan, 11 November: "I'd like to code in Weaken ... Weaken (debuff): Deals 1 less damage per stack with attacks ... Weaken can apply to both sides, it's not a bad soft CC from the foes to apply"; then "Weaken can change till after it's next turn then, instead of round end. Let's use Sapped." So a foe's Sapped laid in its turn reaches the machine's next attack.

table.lasts: Until after its next turn

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex:
All armour is negated.
Exposed Sprites can be targeted regardless of reach.
Sprites are forced to target an Exposed Frame at round start.
Turn Start: Reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: The id is exposure, since exposed names the formation word (and named an aim of the foes' until 17 November); a machine's is exposure_mech in the engine. The machine's half is Ryan's of 15 November, built 16 November: "all armour of all kinds"; "Exposed does not strip the petrel's resistant shield"; "keep the logic where enemies don't try and overkill. That helps keep it fair. So the whole field targets up until predicted death, then the rest pick intent targets as normal"; "Exposed sets the intents, everything after proceeds as normal"; "Lure wins". A session's reads where his words give none: a countdown's pick carried from the round before holds, and a machine out of reach (Phased as the round ended) draws nothing. Still his: whether a machine that stands Exposed may be marked again; built as no, so the whole field's fire comes every other round at most. The aim content called exposed went on 17 November with every aim of a foe's own. The machine's text is a session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: Renews: a timer, a second Expose renewing it to the larger count
table.lasts: Exposed 2, a stack going as each of its carrier's turns starts

entries.name: Empowered
entries.codex:
Attacks Gain:
  Hit: +1 damage dealt per stack ({N}).
Turn End: Reduce stacks by half, rounded down.

design.holes: Every grant is one status on the machine and the stacks add up. A halving rule has no duration, so a buff component grants stacks and no rounds. The name is a placeholder. It halves at END TURN since 16 November (Ryan: "Empowered should decay at the end of turn, clearly, not end of round"), so what a machine gains in the enemy's turn it carries whole into its next; at the round's end until then. One term for both sides since 26 November (Ryan: "'Both' empowereds? There should be only one."): the foes' Empowered, the engine's kindled (an add on a foe's attack where a machine's is an add on its attack's damage), reads as this entry (Terms.ALIASES).

table.stacks: Yes: a damage point a stack
table.lasts: Halves as its turn ends, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Sealed
entries.codex:
+3 Armour.
Cooling disabled.
Turn End: Gain 3 Heat.
Weapons Gain:
  Resolve: Removed.
On Reboot: Removed.

design.holes: One chip, renewing, never stacking: the armour it grants is tied to the form. The numbers are placeholders.

table.stacks: Renews: one seal however often it seals
table.lasts: Until a weapon it fires opens it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Changed Over
entries.codex:
The die rolls the second battery, not the first.
Lasts the battle.

design.holes: A working name and text, Claude's drafts of 11 November for Ryan to rewrite. One chip for the second battery, none for the first.

table.lasts: Until the Changeover turns the die back, or the battle ends

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Hit By Weapon: Consume all stacks. The attacker loses 1 Heat per stack ({N}).

design.holes: Engine id cryoed, since the keyword holds cryo; the player reads Cryo on both.

table.stacks: Yes: the Cryo's number per foe reached; a weapon's hit spends every stack
table.lasts: Until a weapon's hit spends it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Armoured
entries.codex:
+1 Armour per stack ({N}).
Turn Start: Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: The engine id stays braced. One clock on both sides, the opening of its side's next turn (Ryan, 15 November: "The common "end" state between both sides is "start of their next turn.""; 16 November, of a machine's, which went at the round's end until then: "Armoured we should change so its end is symmetrical on both sides. Probably means until "start of its next turn.""). A machine's goes as the round opens, before the foes announce, so no blow lands between its old end and its new one. It takes no rounds from any grant.

table.stacks: Yes: an armour point a stack, every stack going at once
table.lasts: Until its next turn starts

entries.name: Hardened Light
entries.codex:
When Hit: If Shield is up, -1 damage received per stack ({N}).
Shield Broken: Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: Ryan, 18 November: "no innate shield armour. The Pulse grants one Hardened Light at tier 1. Hardened Light only decays when the shield breaks, and has a cap of 3 stacks"; "The reboot breaks it yes. When it breaks, it loses all of them. If it's weak, we'll buff it, but this is the best shape that doesn't add any weird exceptions. It contains high points and low points and that makes it interesting and healthy". Shield armour, never armour, so an Expose leaves it ("It's the only tank not weak to Expose"), and it takes nothing off a blow on bare hull, a tick or a burn. What reopens it: a Purge proving too threatening, which moves it to a resource bar in place of a buff (his word the same day). His name of 17 November; the session's Hardened before it, a stack off each turn start for a day.

table.stacks: Yes: a point off every blow a stack while its shield stands
table.lasts: Until its shield breaks, every stack then

entries.name: Primed
entries.codex:
Attacks Gain:
  Resolve: Apply 1 Ablate per hit to each unit hit, then reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: The third primer since 15 November, beside Charged and Supercooled (Ryan: "give it the same format as cryo ... use a stack on firing"; "Primed - agreed, how many Ablate stacks does each Primed stack apply? Just one, like supercooled?"; one, since Ablate 1 on a gun measures as about the point a Charged stack's Shock does). Until then every blow left a stack of Ablating a stack of Primed, for a buff's rounds on a machine and one move on a foe. A placeholder name.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack a weapon fired, each lending Ablate 1
table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Jammed
entries.codex:
This entry comes up blank.
On Reboot: Removed.

design.holes: Disabled until 15 November (Ryan: "Rename to Jammed"). The engine's own name for an entry switched off, by a jam or by a cooldown, stays disabled.

table.lasts: Until the machine's next turn ends

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.codex:
Commit: Suffer 3 damage per stack ({N}).
On Reboot: Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: The bite is the status's own number in the engine's table, a placeholder.

table.lasts: Until the machine reboots

entries.name: Phased
entries.codex:
Cannot be damaged, targeted or hit by anything.
Round End: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan's mark, 15 November: "New effect: "Cannot be damaged or targeted by anything until the end of this round." We remove the awkward act clause, but still ensure that it cannot be buffed or interacted with by allies until it unphases"; "all sources of Phased should say "at the end of this round, grant Phased.""; and his answer: "it's a safe reboot if you can pull it off. All phased granters need to be gated, it should be earned, with the caveat that you have to survive the current round". Engine ids phased and phasing, the wait a source lays, a buff a Purge takes. Its own heat does not burn it (his ruling, 16 November, on a session's read that had the burn land: "it shouldn't take damage from overheating since we don't need the exception. It does accumulate the stacks, though, which it will feel the round after"). Everything it carries ticks (16 November: "Everything ticks during phased. It doesn't take damage but it's a way of waiting out a debuff. That's why my clause of the self-cleanse and self-purge is our way out if it's broken"), so its Ablating fades a stack a turn and takes nothing, and its Regenerating runs. A Volatile bite and a corrupted entry's bite are blocked with the rest ("I think we block the damage as a feature, and see how bad it is once we have real hull cost pieces that matter"). A session's reads of his words: it may spend on itself, and its Lure turns no pick. His spare clause is held until play asks for it ("If that's too strong, I would add "Remove all buffs and debuffs. Cannot gain any buffs or debuffs while Phased.""). A foe's Phased is built since 17 November, on his yes to the bench's row for the Spectre and the Wraith ("Phased on foes can be less strict since it's balanced around their kit and theme"; 16 November: "Phased foes act"): the engine's effect phase, a move of a foe's own or a step of one, the wait landing as the round ends. Less strict in one way, a session's read: its own side still reaches it. Never the last foe standing, never two rounds running. Until 15 November: cannot act, take damage or be targeted until the round's end, granted at once to a machine yet to act. A session's draft, his to write.

table.lasts: Granted as the round ends, to a machine that stands; until the next round's end

entries.name: Ablate
entries.codex: Turn End: Suffer 1 damage per stack ({N}), then reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: Engine ids ablating (a foe's) and ablating_mech (a machine's). Ryan's rule, 15 November, in the place of Burning as heat on a machine: "hits shield first, I think. Pretty deadly otherwise. Bypasses armour when damaging hull"; "Tick of ablate ignores barrier yes". A Phased machine takes no point and its stack fades all the same, and a Swallowed one's stacks wait (Ryan, 16 November: "Everything ticks during phased. It doesn't take damage but it's a way of waiting out a debuff"; "Swallowed it's out of play so everything should pause"). The foes' numbers are still the ones sized as heat, his to set. A session's draft, his to write.

table.stacks: Yes: the Ablate's number per blow, or as many as the foe's move says
table.lasts: Until the stacks run out: one fades at each tick, as its turn ends (a foe's own action done; the end of the player's turn on a machine)

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex:
May not act.
Turn End: Removed. Gain Numbed equal to stun resist: 1, 2 if massive, 3 if elite, hero or boss.

table.lasts: One turn: this round's, or the next if it has acted

entries.name: Vitriol
entries.codex:
Turn End: Lose 10% of current HP per stack ({N}), rounded down, then reduce stacks by 1.
Cannot reduce HP below 1.

design.holes: Only the funnel-web's passive lays it; a keyword that ever carries it shares the word. Whether a tick passes Guarded is the parts' question, as Ablating's is. The word Corroded is kept for a foe's damage over time on machines.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack per weapon hit on a foe showing no intent on the spider; a tick a stack
table.lasts: A stack fades as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Web Bomb
entries.codex: Round End: Consumed to apply Suppressed to this Sprite and the nearest Sprite to its right in the same rank, or to its left if none.

design.holes: The burst catches the next foe to act beside it in its rank, the one to its left when none stands to its right; on a foe already suppressed it is wasted, and each half feeds the Paradox as the Suppress keyword's does. Named for its piece and its rider no keyword since 15 November (Ryan: "I don't think the rider needs to be listed as a keyword. It's a unique effect, and the debuff can be renamed \"web bomb.\""); the id is the engine's.

table.lasts: Until the round's end, when it bursts

entries.name: Spun Up
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Commit: Consume all stacks to gain +1 damage per stack ({N}).

design.holes: Ryan, 26 November: "Spun up needs to go to 1 at base, the 2 was a holdover from larger numbers", and his line "Weapons Gain: Commit: Consume all stacks to gain +1 damage per stack ({N})". Spent whole by the next weapon, equipment leaving it (26 October).

table.stacks: Yes: +1 damage a stack, every stack spent by the next weapon
table.lasts: Until the next weapon it spends, across turns

entries.name: Ricochet
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Resolve: Hit the target again once per stack ({N}) for 1 damage. No effect of the weapon applies.
Hull Damaged: Reduce stacks by half, rounded down.
Lasts the skirmish.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "Ricochet (buff): After firing a weapon, it hits the primary target 1 more time per stack, dealing 1 damage each time and applying all effects other than area keywords"; "I'm leaving what applies in the ricochets open, if applying unique effects N more times is broken, then we dial it back and explicitly say 'keywords' instead of 'effects'"; 11 November: "Lose half stacks of Ricochet on any hull damage". His first thought, a Ricochet on every foe a weapon hits, he dropped with Sweep. Claude's readings, built on his go and his to move: 1 in place of the entry's number and of its reads of the foe, the firer's adds on it; half rounded down at each blow, bite or overheat that takes hull, so a lone stack is lost; no cap; a buff a Purge takes.

table.stacks: Yes: a strike of 1 more a stack after each shot
table.lasts: The fight; hull damage halves it

entries.name: Essence
entries.codex:
When any Sprite is defeated: Gain 1 Essence.
Skirmish Start: Gain 1 Empowered per 5 Essence.
Round End: If this Frame killed a Sprite this round, gain 1 Empowered per 5 Essence.
Lasts the battle.

design.holes: Ryan's rework of 12 November, Souls then; Essence his name of 15 November ("Rename souls to Essence"). No cap by his call ("as part of the fantasy"), so it is no store, which is capped and wears a bar: an Ability, a chip with its count. The kill's flare is once a round, as it ends, when an attack of the Ammit's killed in it (Ryan, 16 November: "at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy"); once an attack that killed from 12 November until then ("Flaring twice for an AoE is probably wrong, let's make it 'one of more killed' by an attack"), and once for each foe in the first build. The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: Yes: one for every foe that falls in its fight, with no cap
table.lasts: The battle

entries.name: Offhand
entries.codex:
Uses on a Sprite Gain:
  The armament shown.
  Resolve: Switch to the next armament.
Skirmish Start: Switch to the first armament.

design.holes: Ryan, 19 November: "Only its offhand swaps"; "It cycles after a spend"; "remove the manual weapon cycle"; the spends that carry its rider turn it, his answer of the same day. The chip takes its armament's name and line (Beam Rifle, Beam Sword, Beam Shield, and the branches' Saber, Buckler, Bazooka and Pavise), each the passive's or a step's. The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: No: one armament at a time
table.lasts: The fight, turning after each weapon or equipment it aims at a foe

entries.name: Aile Boost
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Indirect.
  Resolve: Consumed.

design.holes: Ryan, 19 November: "Rapid. Next weapon strike gains Indirect reach"; "Next weapon strike -> Next weapon fired. Applies to the whole spend"; "Booster's buff is the booster's name". The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until the next weapon it fires, across turns

entries.name: Aile Blitz
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Indirect.
  Ignores Armour.
  Resolve: Consumed.

design.holes: Ryan, 19 November: "Aile Booster -> Aile Blitzer: 'Rapid. Next weapon strike gains Indirect reach and ignores armour.'"; its name his ("'Aile Blitz'"). The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until the next weapon it fires, across turns

entries.name: Aile Assault
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Indirect.
  Resolve: Consumed.

design.holes: Ryan, 19 November: "Aile Booster -> Aile Assaulter: 'Rapid. Next weapon strike gains Indirect reach. Gain 1 Empowered.'"; its name his ("'Aile Assault'"). The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until the next weapon it fires, across turns

entries.name: Parry
entries.codex:
Counts damage prevented by Armour and Barrier from Sprite hits this round.
Turn Start: The first weapon hit this turn gains +1 damage per 2 damage counted.
Resolve: If a weapon was used, consumed.
Turn End: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 19 November: "Parry: 'The first weapon fired next turn gains bonus damage equal to half of all damage blocked by this machine this round (rounded down).'" What is blocked, his answer that day: what a Barrier and armour keep off, never the shield's soak. His of the same day, on the bonus: "Can we change it to 'next strike' instead?" (every strike of the next weapon, his first wording, made a busted area of the rifle that follows the shield), the next strike the spend's first blow by his strike order. Claude's reading: the count runs from the moment it is gained. It pays half the blow a Barrier stops, so a boss's biggest blow pays most, beside his taste of October ("No reward for being struck that scales with the enemy's blows"): his of 19 November, "The duelist is supposed to be a boss-killer, and this is a tier-3 capstone, yes, so it can be powerful". The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: No: one Parry, counting through its round, then its return, its number half of what it counted, spent whole by the next weapon
table.lasts: Its round, then the next turn until a weapon fires

entries.name: Essence Flare
entries.codex:
Empowered on any unit is not reduced.
Round End: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 12 November: "No Empowered decays this round. And I mean none, not ally or enemy." Pinned Empowered until 15 November, a chip on every unit holding Empowered and the round's own rule; then his: "This is not pinned empowered, this is an Ammit specific buff. I would give it to the Ammit only, even though it affects the whole battlefield"; "Grants the no-decay state which is represented as a buff on the Ammit called Essence Flare." That a Purge ends the hold follows from its being a buff.

table.lasts: Until the round's end

entries.name: Sustained Recoil
entries.codex: Max 5 stacks. At 5 stacks, the next weapon hit deals double damage.

design.holes: Ryan, 26 November: "Sustained Recoil (Resource): Max 5 stacks. At 5 stacks, the next weapon hit deals double damage." Every weapon hit, an area's included, adds a stack; the hit that finds five consumes them all. Its bar has five cells, glowing and pulsing whole while full (his: "indicating the next shot is the sixth"). The six-shot count it replaced (shots) is git's.

table.stacks: Yes: one a weapon hit, up to five
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Brittle
entries.codex:
When Hit: +1 damage received per stack ({N}).
Turn Start: Reduce stacks by half, rounded down.

design.holes: Engine ids brittled (a foe's) and brittled_mech (a machine's). Flak on a foe (Wainwright & Sutler's on-hit, 19 October) and Crushed on a machine (the World Eater's pin, 4 November, Monster Hunter's Defense Down by archetype; Ryan: "that inflicts Defense Down in game, something we don't have") until 15 November, folded on Ryan's mark ("We could consider making this one symmetrical and folding it into Flak as well, changing the name so it works on both sides") and his "agreed, brittle". One clock, the halving: a machine's stood whole through the next round until then, so a foe's Brittle 1 was the pack's for the turn it was laid in and gone by the next, and a foe lays 2 at the least since 16 November (Ryan: "Buffs and debuffs that decay at end of round should just have a minimum of 2"; the validator holds a foe's moves to it, and our own pieces are not held to it: "The minimum 2 is different for the player since they can sequence. So I wouldn't make it a blanket rule"). Adds before multiplies and before armour, to a weapon's blow of 0 too (Ryan, 25 October: "Flak and overcharge exist in part to get past armour"), so a Shocked foe carrying Brittle takes blow plus Brittle, doubled. Numbers are placeholders; Brittle beside Empowered at a point a stack each may read too strong, the two read together on the Prairie Dog's rows. A session's draft, his to write. It halves as its carrier's turn starts since 16 November (his four places, Brittle with what ends at a turn's start; at the round's end until then, no blow apart).

table.stacks: Yes: N a hit from a Brittle N piece, N a blow from a foe's Brittle N; a point more on every blow it takes, a stack
table.lasts: Halves as its turn starts, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex:
This entry is blank for the rest of the battle. Passive bonuses still apply. Passive abilities do not.
After the battle: an Integrated component is rebuilt, a hardpoint's component is lost.

design.holes: No foe carries Destroy yet, so nothing is destroyed in play (Ryan, 15 November: "Only promoted form or superboss-level so we're not tuning the economy around it. No longer a general rule"). The campaign's hangar screen is not built.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Four slots, one a column. Front-rank foes fill these. Always in Direct reach.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Four slots behind the front. Back-rank foes hold these.

entries.name: Mine
entries.codex:
Uses aimed at this Sprite by the Frame that laid it add their damage and riders to the Mine.
When defeated: The Mine goes off, hitting every Sprite around it for 1 damage per stack ({N}), with its riders.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "the lammergeier basically converts all hits to AoE hits, at the cost of a delay until Death". One Mine a spend at a flat 2 ("then look at per hit later if it's weak"); its riders the spend's whole result on the foe ("the mine should take the entire result of the spend, then apply it. So a 3-hit flak that burns 1 per hit if the target is under 50% HP, would result in adding a 2 damage mine with 3 flak, and 0-3 burn"), every hit's stacks as its machine deepened and doubled them and a gated keyword where its gate held ("if a gate is met when fired only, then apply it"); the numbered ones add up and the rest ride once; Chain rides as its arcs (Claude's lean, which he took); in the enemy's turn a Mine's Disrupt does nothing; a Suppress rides as fired, each foe the blast meets judging its own Numbed (Claude's read; Ryan: "Your reads are correct"). A mark the team laid: a Ward turns it away, a foe's cleanse takes it, the Paradox counts it. A foe taken into a merge hands its Mine to the merger.

table.stacks: Yes: its damage, every spend adding to it, one Mine a foe
table.lasts: The fight, until the foe falls or the Syrinx Drone detonates it

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Some of the rank and file are massive, the treants and the sandworms among them, and some elites and bosses.

design.holes: Spread treats it as a front-rank neighbour; Penetrate finds nothing behind it.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Move in hexes: how far a machine goes in an action, a step a hex. Water costs a ground machine two; a hovercraft and a flyer cross it at one; walls are the flyer's alone.

design.holes: Every chassis's move is a placeholder set by size and role; what crossing water and walls is worth is the pricing run's to read (28 October).

entries.name: Walk
entries.codex: The map shows where every pack will walk on the enemy's turn, worked out from where your machines' plans end: a pusher toward the gate, a hunter toward its prey. Packs walk through your machines and the wrecks, never ending a walk on one, so nothing you do stops one.

design.holes: A pack with no way to the gate waits, and the map says so.

entries.name: Fight
entries.codex: Tap a pack to attack it. One pack is one fight: nothing joins it, and you commit the machines beside it. Orders onto several packs play one fight at a time, each resolved before the next and fought to its end; a machine that fought, won or lost, is spent until your next turn.

entries.name: Spent
entries.codex: A machine that has fought this turn is spent: it cannot move or fight again until your next turn. A machine whose passive grants a second action has two before it is spent.

entries.name: Carry
entries.codex: A machine that carries (the Swallowtail's Muster Deck) lifts the machines on the hexes beside it when it moves: they travel as a ring round it and land as a block, each where it rode from it, keeping whatever move and action they had. It cannot stop where a rider would land on a hex it cannot stand on (NO ROOM). A caught machine does not ride.

design.holes: A landing animation or a redistribution on landing may come later.

entries.name: Caught
entries.codex: A machine a hunter has caught fights it first on your turn, before any other fight, and cannot move until then. Others in range may join that fight. It is fought to its end: the hunter falls or the machine is wrecked.

entries.name: Engage range
entries.codex: A hunter catches what stands beside where its walk ends: the engage range, one hex, the same reach every unit has on the map, so a machine joins a fight on a pack beside it and a hunter catches its prey beside it. No ring is drawn: a hunter wears a chip with the machine it comes for. No pack joins a fight; one pack is one fight.

design.holes: One number in the engine, the engage range (Unit.ENGAGE_RANGE, a placeholder: adjacency), serving the machines' reach onto a pack, the hunters' catch and the ring drawn; the hunters' pounce of two (Ryan, 29 October, "wolfs pounce") retired 10 November with the body blocking, so the catch is "the same melee engage range as everyone else" (Ryan); no foe or composition carries a ring since 8 November.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries.codex: A pack pushes unless its composition hunts. A pusher walks toward the gate and threatens nothing else. A hunter locks one machine, by its caveat (the nearest, weakest, strongest or slowest), puts its tag on it and walks toward it; when it ends its walk beside its prey it has caught it, and that fight comes first on your next turn. A caught machine cannot move until the fight, and is caught again while the hunter lives. A prey that keeps its distance is safe, and so is one no hex beside can be stood on that turn: its prey is the only machine a hunter catches, and nothing stands in for it.

design.holes: Push and hunt are the only behaviours; the hunters' caveats are placeholders.

entries.name: Pack
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a pack: a composition on one hex, its members listed on a hold, wearing its lead's picture, hunting when its composition says so, walking at its slowest member's pace. Its hold says first how many machines it is a fight for, its threat rating; a pusher walks to a segment of the wall of its own. A fight is the one pack you attack. A boss is one unit on one hex.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: Every unit covers one hex, the boss included: it is occupied, counts for range, and is a tap target. The gate and the rift are wider structures.

design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A pack that ends its walk beside a gate hex or a wall hex strikes the gate. A tear is a mouth, not a structure: its hex can be walked and stood on.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: At a peak of Rift Pressure the rift sends 2 packs, each to a stretch of the wall of its own, and every tear open before the peak sends 2 to the wall near it. The pack for a stretch is the next of its threat rating the domain has, the lead domain's and the guest's in turn. A spawn lands on the nearest free hex to its mouth with no Frame beside it, the rift's outside its shell on the side they are headed, at the end of the enemy's turn, so you see it and its walk for a whole turn and nothing lands on top of a detachment.

entries.name: Composition
entries.codex: What the rift sends and what stands on the field when a battle starts: a patrol (a few foes, a fight for one machine or a pair), a formation (the body's fight), an elite leading its own, or a boss's escort. A composition is one pack on one hex: its members, listed on a hold, unpack into the fight together and come back by member. Each domain writes its compositions by tier, each dealt across a band of the ramp; the ramp sets how many stand at the start, never how thick they are.

design.holes: Each tier's compositions are partitioned from its list as placeholders for Ryan's marks; the escorts are written for their bosses by tier.

entries.name: Patrol
entries.codex: The small composition: a few foes, a fight for one machine or for a pair, the threat rating its hold shows. Its threat rating says where it makes for: 1 the wall's ends, 2 between the ends and the middle.

design.holes: The tier-one patrols read as a lone starter's fight on the greedy rung, not a tenth of its hull (docs/measurements.md, 30 October); their sizes are Ryan's to mark.

entries.name: Formation
entries.codex: The body's composition: a fight for three machines, the threat rating its hold shows. It makes for the middle of the wall. 1 stands before it at the start (2 from Convergence 3, 3 from 8). A domain's tier writes its formations; the lead's and the guest's come in turn.

design.holes: The word also names the skirmish's two ranks; the context tells them apart.

entries.name: Tear
entries.codex: A mouth beside the rift's. At a peak of Rift Pressure the ramp's count of tears (one; two from Convergence 8) open on a row a few past the rift (row 4 at twelve deep), each peak's a row nearer the wall and never beside it, as far from the rift and the other tears as the row allows, and every tear open before the peak sends 2 packs to the wall near it. A tear opens a peak before it first sends, so where the next flood comes from is known an interval ahead. Tears stay open and never close.

design.holes: Drawn as a first cut for the phone; its mark and its opening are to judge running (RIFTGATE_PEAK_DEBUG=1 peaks every enemy turn).

entries.name: Seam
entries.codex: The flattening's edge: a circle about the rift, four hexes out as a battle opens and half a hex wider every round, stopping at the foot of the wall. It is a picture alone: no rule reads the ground inside it, and a tear opens wherever its own row has room.

design.holes: Its start and its growth a round are placeholders for his eye (Bleed.seam_start_hex, Bleed.seam_grow_hex; the map tuner moves both).

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Open ground. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Open ground, the same as plain: the road is art. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Forest and scrub. Every machine and pack crosses it.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Rubble. Every machine and pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet; what terrain does in a fight is section 12's question.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Tracks, walkers and wheels wade it, a hex costing two of their move; hovercraft and flyers cross it at full pace. Packs wade it as the ground machines do; a winged pack crosses it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet (section 12). Each map shape lays its own water (a fat river with its narrows, a delta's channels, ponds, a pond, the gorge's flooded channels, or none: the city has none). Since 29 October the horde wades it as the ground machines do, so water slows a crossing and never walls it; the crossing guarantee binds the walls.

entries.name: Crags
entries.codex: Rock spikes. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Mesas
entries.codex: Flat-topped rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Towers
entries.codex: Dead skyscrapers. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Cliffs
entries.codex: A wall of rock. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Chasms
entries.codex: A sheer drop. Impassable, except to flyers and winged packs.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Crosses everything, water and walls included. It flies over machines and packs, and they pass under it, but nothing stops on another's hex.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Skims water at full pace; walls stop it.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Legs. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Tracked
entries.codex: Tracks. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: Wheeled
entries.codex: Wheels. Wades water at half pace.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A wall segment's upgrade the foes can strike, the gate's flanking guns first and turrets later. Not on the field yet.

design.holes: No die and no rule yet: how gate defences work is section 12's question.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires on every attack, after its number is read. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, multiply the printed number alone before any buff (the Kite's double, on an unhurt foe), or set a minimum damage.

entries.name: On struck
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when a foe's blow lands on this machine, a time a blow, whatever the blow dealt: it gains heat, or lays a status on the striker. A blow that wrecks the machine gains and lays nothing.

design.holes: Its carriers the Echidna's Sonic Needles (Ryan, 20 November: "getting struck by one, grants that foe a stack of Sonic Needle") and the Nemesis's heat (24 November: "When Hit: gain 1 heat"). The codex is a session's draft.

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains shield from any source, with the amount gained; it may shed heat or grant a status, never raise more shield.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On shielding an ally
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine spends a shield component on an ally, with the shield's size; it may shed the ally's heat or grant the ally a status, never raise more shield. It never fires for a shield on itself.

design.holes: Fires on the spend, whatever the shield gained, so a shield die on a topped-up ally still does its other work.

entries.name: On buffing an ally
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine spends a piece of equipment on an ally, once for each ally it lands on, whatever the equipment did; it may take some of the ally's heat onto this machine. It never fires for equipment on itself.

design.holes: Its carrier the Puffin's pull (Ryan, 11 November: "Using an equipment on an ally moves some of its heat to the Puffin"; 19 November: "I think 4 for the Puffin"). The piece that passes heat fires none: its heat goes the other way. The codex is a session's draft.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains heat, with the amount; it may raise shield or grant a status, never add heat.

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once as the skirmish begins, before the first roll: a shield, a vent, a status.

design.holes: The Ammit's passive uses it.

entries.name: On foe status
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when any foe gains a status, whoever applied it: once for each status a spend puts on a foe, however many strikes or stacks (an application, not a stack). Never for Paradox, nor for the Suppressed a Paradox causes, and Numbed is no status. Effects: paradox (the foe gains a stack of Paradox; at the count it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears).

entries.name: On applying stacks
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine applies stacks of a status to anyone: a foe's Ablate (from an Ablate or from Primed), an ally's or its own buff, its own Empowered from a kill. Effects: add_stacks (so many stacks more, flat or for every so much heat the machine carries). Never for Numbed, which is exempt from every interaction.

design.holes: Shocked and Suppressed are not stacks, so it never touches them.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine loses hull: to a blow, a bite or an overheat.

design.holes: The hook for the pinned berserker idea too; the Nemesis's Berserker, a heat for hull lost (24 November).

entries.name: On a blow blocked
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once for every blow of this machine's weapons that a living foe's armour or Barrier takes whole, each foe's of an area and each strike's.

design.holes: The Nemesis's Breaker, two heat a blow blocked (Ryan, 11 November: per blow, "that lets it scrap against the comp its supposed to"; on its passive from 23 to 24 November, its branch's since).

entries.name: Turn Start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as this machine's turn starts, after a reboot's recovery and before its die rolls.

design.holes: The Whip Scorpion's Obliterator (Ryan, 24 November: "Turn Start: Gain 1 heat"). The codex is a session's draft.

entries.name: On gaining a Barrier
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as this machine gains a Barrier, from its own equipment or an ally's.

design.holes: The Wild Boar's Juggernaut Drive (Ryan, 11 November: "After gaining Barrier, its next weapon attack gains Breach"; ignores armour since 15 November).

entries.name: On a kill
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once after an attack of this machine's that killed, however many foes fell to it, chains and spills included: a status, a shield (the Kite's, recharged whole) or a vent.

entries.name: At the end of a round it killed in
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as the round ends, after the enemy's turn, for a machine whose own attack killed in that round: once, however many foes fell and however many attacks felled them (the Ammit's flare).

design.holes: Ryan, 16 November, the Ammit's passive in his words: "At the start of the skirmish, or at the end of a round where the Ammit killed at least one enemy, the Essences Flare, granting 1 Empowered per 5 Essences it holds." A kill is an attack's, as the kill trigger counts it; a machine wrecked in the enemy's turn fires nothing.

entries.name: On a foe killed
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires as a death check counts a kill in this machine's fight, whoever or whatever made it, an ally's blow, an Ablate tick and a Mine's blast among them: a status, once for each foe that fell (the Ammit's Essence), or a shield gain like any (the Buzzard's).

design.holes: Built 12 November for the Ammit's Souls. It fires once for each foe that falls, which is what the trigger is: no effect opts into the count. A foe getting back up, a part and a Bomb's burst are no kill and fire nothing.

entries.name: On damaging a foe
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after a spend of this machine's weapons that took HP off a foe, however many foes it hurt: a status, a shield or a vent. An effect may fire once a round only (the Skua's stack of Ricochet).

design.holes: Built for the Skua's rewrite (Ryan, 11 November: "Damaging an enemy grants it a stack of Ricochet (once per turn)"). The stack lands after the spend that earned it, so none of that spend's shots bounce off it. The once-a-round gate is the effect's own (once: round), open to any effect an event fires.

entries.name: On use
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once after every use of this machine's components, its hits all done (Resolve), whatever the component: a status of its own (the Cassowary's Deadeye II, a Sustained Recoil). A blank entry is no use and fires nothing.

design.holes: Built for the Cassowary's Deadeye II (Ryan, 26 November: "All Components gain: Resolve: Gain 1 Sustained Recoil"). It fires after the use's own reads: the Negentropy Spinner's advance reads the count before its Resolve adds one. A stack it lays on a store stops at the store's cap. Only stack_status runs on it today.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the machines' dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. A pouch of three: a fourth forces a use or a discard. One comes from a Fracture's pick, and a starting stock chosen in the hangar restocks every battle. It expires when the rift closes.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: Not built: a Fracture brings no prize, and whether one should is open. If it comes, a Fracture grants one, unweighted by domain: one of three, a battle-long modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon (an extra reroll a round).

design.holes: Built without one (Ryan, 24 October: maybe not warranted at all); decided after the meter is played, with the economy pass.

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Tier
entries.codex: The hard scaling: a rift's tier is locked as the rift opens and sets the kind of battle: who comes, the sizes of its compositions, the Fractures to the Rupture, how many elites and which, the boss's numbers and escort. The Convergence's tier rises one every four; a rift keeps the tier it opened at, so an old rift never hardens by waiting.

design.holes: Shown on the front's card when the mission map comes; today the campaign runs headless.

entries.name: Ramp
entries.codex: The soft scaling under the tier, never shown: the Convergence as it stands when a battle starts sets how many compositions stand on the field at the start and which of the tier's variants are dealt, how fast Rift Pressure fills, how many tears open at a peak and how far each peak's open toward the wall. It scales no pack. It rises with the run, the same for every open front, and never resets.

design.holes: One table of placeholders (sim/ramp.gd), read by the campaign runner and moved on Ryan's word; the timer's 12 reads as the old clock's number (docs/measurements.md, 30 October).

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex:
Resolve: This entry goes dark for the rest of the round and the next {N} rounds.
A dark entry can be rolled but not used.

design.holes: A price as heat is. Counted after the round of the spend since 12 November (Ryan: "change the count so 1 is how I intended"; the round of the spend counted from 14 October, when a weapon's 1 cost nothing, the die spent for the round anyway). The city's battlefield abilities count their own cooldowns in phases.

entries.name: Gather
entries.codex: Resolve: Every other Sprite's Mine merges into the target's Mine.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "moves all mines to a single target, and Exposes that target. The Expose rider will effectively create an AoE expose mine, which we can try and see if it's dangerous." Its Expose is its keyword, so the Mine it gathers carries Expose. A Ward on the target turns the gather away.

entries.name: Detonate
entries.codex: Resolve: The target's Mine goes off, including this use's addition.

design.holes: Ryan, 9 November: "Deals a small amount of damage and detonates a foe's combined mine immediately ... The small chip damage makes it add a stack first. Try without a cooldown first." Its chip strike spends a Shock on the target, so a Shock doubles the chip, never the Mine.

entries.name: On itself
entries.codex: Resolve: This Frame gains the status shown. Where shown: once per Sprite hit, up to the cap shown.

design.holes: Its carrier the Storm Petrel's Hardlight Pulse (Ryan, 18 November): Hardened Light 1, up to 3, printed on the piece; its branches take it further through the pipeline (self_status): the Defence direction a Ward and a cap of 4, then a stack for each foe hit and a cap of 5, the Striker's Charged 1 and then 2. Its first form the lock's own Regenerating on itself (regenerates, 30 October to 17 November). Machine buffs and a Ward, never a Barrier, which keeps its pieces and its cooldown.

entries.name: An ally's action
entries.codex: Resolve: If the target Frame's die is used, spend {N} rerolls to reroll it onto a different entry. It can act again.

design.holes: Its price is the lever if it reads as Rapid embodied in a machine (the bible's Kestrel row); the order is the play, the ally spending first.

entries.name: Rolls its die
entries.codex: Resolve: The target's die rerolls onto a different entry. A used die cannot reroll.

entries.name: Rerolls a kill
entries.codex: Resolve: If any Sprite hit was defeated, gain {N} rerolls.

entries.name: Grants a reroll
entries.codex: Resolve: Gain {N} rerolls.

design.holes: The Rallied buff until 15 November (Ryan's mark: "This doesn't need to be a temporary buff or a keyword ... We can communicate by highlighting the reroll button as part of the preview, if one will be granted"; the grant passing the round's two: "allow it"). A reroll the Horn grants still counts toward the Muster when spent on the carrier. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of kit on a machine, and one entry on its die. There is no generic kit: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the machine can do.

design.holes: Multi-slot components were set aside as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

entries.name: Integrated component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis. Always on the die and uses no hardpoint. Cannot be removed, sold or built. No other Frame carries it.

design.holes: Never bought open. Locked pieces are powerful and unique, never blueprints, so no hardpoint stocks one and none carries a tier (the validator holds it; ContentDB.component_tier answers 0).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

entries.name: Module
entries.codex: Kit inside the machine, not on its die: a few numbers up or down, and at most one rule of its own. A chassis has its module slots (two, three on the Clydesdale), and a module is never spent: it is always working.

design.holes: Fitted in the harness and the quick campaign's hangar: the campaign's roster, the loot that drops them and its hangar wait for the economy pass and the hangar screen.

entries.name: On injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when a blow would destroy a component (a foe's Destroy, any of it on the hull). Effects: no_destroy (the component holds instead of being destroyed).

entries.name: Armour
entries.codex: A chassis number taken off every blow that reaches the hull, flat, never a percentage: a blow on bare hull and what passes a shield alike. A blow at or under the armour does nothing to the hull. Shield is not armoured: a blow on shield costs the shield its full damage.

design.holes: Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Strike order
entries.codex: Foes strike in the order they stand: front rank left to right, then the back rank. Each blow is resolved on its own against the shield standing at that moment, so which foe strikes first decides what a small shield takes. A pack stands as its composition's grid has it; a boss's fight and a final stand heaviest hitters first from the left.

entries.name: Aim
entries.codex:
How a Sprite picks its target at round start, shown as its arrow.
Strongest: most Hull plus Shield.
Weakest: least Hull plus Shield.
Hottest: most Heat.
Most buffed: most Buff stacks.
No word: any Frame. Ties are random.
Never targets a Frame its hits would already wreck while another stands.

design.holes: Content: aim on a move aimed at one machine, never on a foe (Ryan, 17 November: "the heat target is a property of the attack, not the dragon itself"; his go on the three words the same day: "if it's the strongest/weakest/hottest table from above, then yes I agree and you can go ahead"); when on a move is the condition that lets a foe pick it, and a special never fires twice running. The strongest and the weakest have no carrier yet, and the most buffed is a session's keep for the Djinn's Unmake (the bible's section 12). The codex and the words on a move's target line are a session's drafts, his to write in his terminology pass.

entries.name: Self-Destruct
entries.codex: Resolve: This Sprite is removed. It cannot return.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. A self-destructing foe counts as a kill like any other.

entries.name: Every Frame
entries.codex: Hits every Frame. No target, so Lure cannot move it.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. Its number is per machine, so a move with it is priced well under a single blow from the same foe. The name is a working one.

entries.name: Last Act
entries.codex: When defeated: Use this move at once. A single-target move hits the Frame that killed it, or nothing if no Frame did.

design.holes: Content: on_death.blow, an attack's shape (name, factor, strikes, keywords), beside or instead of a split. The Gargantuan King's Meteor (30 October). A short list of steps since 16 November, on Ryan's mark of 15 November ('foes who, say buff others on death, or debuff on death'): the blow may carry also, and on_death.act is one special in a blow's place with its own also, each an effect a fall may do (Foe.FALL_EFFECTS). Carriers of more than a blow since 17 November, on his yes to the bench: the Mandragora line's scream, the Gorgon's dying gaze, the Salamander's embers and the Lich's, which takes back the readiness it gave (unready_all, a fall's by sense). The codex is a session's draft for them; it and the term's word are his ('maybe rename to something more interesting'). A single blow lands on the machine that made the kill since 17 November, as a curse does (Ryan, of the Dread Knight's Death Throes: 'yes, hit its killer, if it has one'); it followed the foe's own pick until then.

entries.name: Parts
entries.codex: A core and its parts. While every part stands, the core is Guarded. A defeated part may grow back. When the core is defeated, its parts are defeated.

design.holes: Content: parts (foe ids), guard (all or any), regrow_parts (rounds). Parts are found by pack and type, one deep, and each takes a cell of its pack's grid. The Fallen Weapon's two eyes and the Obsidian Tyrant's rider (30 October); a move may open once a part has fallen (part_fallen).

entries.name: Countdown
entries.codex:
Lands {N} rounds after it is announced. Nothing hits while it gathers.
Suppress delays it 1 round. Disrupt cancels it.

design.holes: The foe stays on the field while it gathers; its pick holds while the machine stands, and a Lure moves it.

entries.name: Follow-up
entries.codex: Names the move its Sprite announces next round. Suppress or Disrupt on the first cancels the second. Once announced, the second can be Suppressed but not Disrupted.

design.holes: Content: then, on the first move, naming the second (30 October). One deep: a follow-up names none of its own and comes only after the move that names it, never by the roll. A borrowed swing with nothing taken is no follow-up, and the roll decides. Off the player's list since 15 November (Ryan: "I don't think we need to explicitly spell this out for the player. A backend pattern is ok, and it will become obvious through play and mastery by the player"): the engine's pattern, with no term and no row in the list; a move's own readout still says what it names next.

entries.name: Grudge
entries.codex: +1 damage per Sprite the team has killed this skirmish.

design.holes: The Pilgrim's Karma (30 October), the Tonberry's Everyone's Grudge under a name of ours. Content: per_kill on an attack, the points a kill. Every fall counts but a foe that went whole (a burst, a part falling with its core) and one taken in by a merge.

entries.name: Sprite move
entries.codex: Each round every Sprite picks a move and a target before your turn, shown on its intent chip. Attack damage is the Sprite's attack times the move's factor.

design.holes: A foe's whole brain is its weighted draw and its pick; none plans ahead.

entries.name: Vents all
entries.codex: Commit: Reduce Heat to 0. +X damage per Y Heat vented, as shown on the entry.

design.holes: Only the first shot of a chain fires the heat.

entries.name: Fires the shield
entries.codex: Commit: Reduce Shield to 0. +X damage per Y Shield spent, as shown on the entry.

design.holes: Its carrier the Buzzard's Shield-burner Cannon (Ryan, 18 November: it breaks the shield, and no zap rides it: "It can't, since the shield will be empty"). Never beside Vents all on one entry (the validator). The codex is a session's draft.

entries.name: Passes heat
entries.codex: Resolve: Move all of this Frame's Heat to the target. The target gains 1 stack of the shown status per Y Heat moved, rounded down.

design.holes: Its carrier the Puffin's dump (Ryan, 11 November: "A locked piece can transfer the Puffins heat to another unit along with a buff based on heat moved"; "just allies"; 19 November, Empowered for every 2: "that needs data"). An ally its heat takes past the maximum burns as the turn ends, his "forcing an overheat". The codex is a session's draft.

entries.name: Grows with missing HP
entries.codex: Commit: +X damage per Y HP the target is missing, as shown on the entry.

design.holes: Both numbers are the entry's own (power_per_missing and per_missing), placeholders.

entries.name: Finisher
entries.codex: Commit: If the target is at or below half Max HP, double base damage.

design.holes: A working name. The Coriolis Accelerator's slope as one step (Ryan, 11 November: "is there a way to make the pinion driver simpler but fill the same purpose"); its factor is the entry's own (finisher), a placeholder.

entries.name: Fixed
entries.codex: Only the specified component may be used.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November, for the third case in a week (the Nemesis's Rage, the Mole's burrow, the Whip Scorpion's reboot that puts the Death Ray on its die): "It might want a keyword: 'Fixed: Knuckles of Fury'. Fixed: Only the specified component may be used." The kit word it would have met became Integrated the same day ("I'd rather change Fixed a chassis locked components to Integrated"). A word of the text: each piece's own engine path holds its die to its one component.

entries.name: Gated
entries.codex: The keyword applies only to Sprites that meet its condition at Commit.

design.holes: Suppress alone carries a gate today. A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: Consumes
entries.codex:
Hit: If a weapon, consume all stacks of the named status on the Sprite hit. +{N} damage per stack consumed.
Commit: If equipment, consume up to {N} of the named count from this Frame. Gain 1 stack of the granted status per one consumed.
Equipment cannot be used with nothing to consume.

design.holes: A mine laid from it eats its arrival's stacks. The equipment's form is the Quintessence Tap's (12 November, the Soul Siphon then), the engine's spends and spends_up_to; its text is a session's draft.

entries.name: Ablates its firer
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Ablate to this Frame.
