design.holes: A working name for Ryan's name pass. It was fuel for a machine that wanted heat while a machine's Burning was heat; since Ablate (15 November) it is a price alone, the component pass's to read.

entries.name: Ignores Armour
entries.codex: Armour does not reduce the damage.

design.holes: Ryan, 15 November, with Breach cut on both sides: "I would remove Breach from the player's side. Ignores armour can be an explicitly written out property"; "the player armour piercing pieces should be higher tier, obviously, or gated, I think. Else they become obvious best faces for certain domains". On the Ammit's Soulcutter Talons, the Wild Boar's next weapon after a Barrier, and the Overclocked Railgun, whose tier is the component pass's. A session's draft, his to write.

entries.name: Empties the hopper
entries.codex:
Commit: Consume all Ore. Hit once per Ore consumed. No Ore is gained from these hits.
Cannot be used without Ore.

design.holes: Ryan, 20 November: "Empties the hopper, striking once for every load emptied. Grants no Ore." "Fragmenter is a dead face with no Ore." The numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Braces
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Armoured to this Frame.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it; the stacks are a placeholder.

entries.name: Strikes
entries.codex: Hits per use. Each hit deals full damage and is reduced by Armour separately.

design.holes: Heat is paid once per use, not per strike.

entries.name: Always on
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Its effects change a machine's numbers or a component's properties while a condition holds, rather than firing on an event: add_stat and multiply_stat on hull, shield, heat maximum, armour, move, cooling or shield regen; add_damage_taken and multiply_damage_taken on every incoming blow; set_reach on a component (direct or indirect while a condition holds); suppress, which turns off another effect by id or tag; and the rules a passive writes on its machine's entries, the star on the die: ignore_armour, and spillover (the Overrun Gearing's: damage past a kill in the front rank carries into the foe behind it in the same column, nothing standing behind a massive foe).

design.holes: Every read asks the pipeline; nothing is written to a stat or a component, so an effect that is gone stops answering. A static reach rule cannot be conditioned on reach.

entries.name: Order of operations
entries.codex: Everything that changes a number goes through one pipeline, in one order. Sources: the chassis passive, each fitted component's passive and each fitted module (until refitted), skirmish rewards (until the battle ends), buffs and debuffs (until the skirmish ends, or until the end of a given round). First suppression, shortest-lived source to longest: a live effect that suppresses another by id or tag turns it off, and a suppressed effect suppresses nothing. Then the gate: an effect takes part only if it is live, its trigger fires now, its condition holds, and, for an ability, its component is not destroyed (a destroyed component keeps its stat bonuses and loses its abilities). Then adds, all sources summed; then multiplies, all sources multiplied; then floors and caps; then overrides, where the shortest-lived source wins and the latest granted breaks ties. In an attack, the number (with what fired heat or a target's missing hull adds) comes before the pipeline's adds and multiplies; nothing is ever stored as a total: every read asks again, so an effect that is gone stops answering. Statuses stack: the same status granted again adds stacks instead of a second copy; an add is worth its value per stack and a multiply is applied once per stack; each ends on one of four clocks, its owner's turn starting, its turn ending, the round ending or its spending, a ticking one paying its point a stack and losing a stack as its owner's turn ends, and is gone at zero.

design.holes: Refit (the hangar) is what changes loadout-scoped effects; not built.

entries.name: Rage
entries.codex:
Immune to all Debuffs.
Fixed: Knuckles of Fury
Reboot disabled.
At 0 Heat: Consumed to Reboot immediately.

design.holes: Ryan, 23 November: "When the Nemesis starts its turn with heat at or over max, it gains the unpurgable status Rage: Remove all debuffs on self. Immune to all debuffs. The only component available is Knuckles of Fury"; "Rage ends when the Nemesis' heat reaches zero, at which point it immediately reboots, regardless of how it got there." Its debuffs are the statuses a foe lays on a machine, the ones a Cleanse lifts. Its heat comes from the blows it takes and its own blows a foe's armour or Barrier takes whole, by the rules its rage was banked by from 11 November. The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until its heat reaches nothing, when it reboots

entries.name: Ore
entries.codex: Machine store, the Honey Badger's hopper: every foe its weapons damage puts an Ore in it, up to three, and every raise its upgrades grant adds to that. Its Bullion Fragmenter empties it, a strike for every Ore, and puts none back. Lasts the skirmish; never decays, and no cleanse or Purge touches it.

design.holes: Ryan, 20 November: "Damaging a foe grants one stack of Ore (max 3). At 3, base armour increases by 1 (represented by an ability chip)." The engine id stays hopper. What the Ore is worth is the Ore chip (ore_plate), an Ability. The four loads and their Armoured of 31 October and 10 November are git's.

table.stacks: Yes: a load a foe its weapons damage (the claw's two), up to 4; two spent a shot
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Ore
entries.codex: At 3 Ore, base Armour increases by 1.

design.holes: Ryan, 20 November: "It's no longer cleansable, represented as an Ore ability chip." Its stacks are the armour, set from the Ore held (Effects._plate).

table.stacks: Yes: its stacks are the armour, set from the Ore held
table.lasts: While the hopper holds the Ore, the skirmish at most

entries.name: Scorched
entries.codex:
Uses on a Sprite Gain:
  Commit: +1 Heat per stack ({N}).
Turn End: Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: Placeholder numbers.

table.lasts: Until the end of the player's turn, every stack at once

entries.name: Overheated
entries.codex:
Stacks equal Heat above Max Heat.
Turn End: Lose 1 Hull per stack ({N}). The first time since the last Reboot, reduce Shield to 0.
On Reboot: Reduce stacks to 0.
Cannot be cleansed.

design.holes: The reboot's (Ryan, 13 November: "an uncleanseable debuff on the unit, a stack for every point of heat"), read off the gauge and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write. The hull a stack burns is the trial's OVERHEAT dial, one the game's.

table.stacks: Yes: a point of heat past the maximum each
table.lasts: Until the heat is back under the maximum, or the machine reboots

entries.name: Broken
entries.codex:
Applied when Shield reaches 0. Shield cannot be gained.
Removed when a Reboot restores Shield.
Cannot be cleansed.

design.holes: The reboot's (Ryan, 13 November: "the unit cannot gain shield by any method"; "you can break yourself"), a state of the machine and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write.

table.lasts: Until the machine's reboot brings its shield back

entries.name: Rebooting
entries.codex:
Applied by dragging the die of a Frame that has used nothing this turn onto REBOOT. Shield and Heat drop to 0 at once.
Turn Start: Consumed to restore Shield to max and remove Broken.

design.holes: The reboot (Ryan, 13 November; folded in 15 November), a state of the machine and no status of the engine's table. A session's draft, his to write.

table.lasts: Through the enemy's turn, until the next round opens

entries.name: Enraged
entries.codex:
Attacks Gain:
  Hit: +1 damage dealt per stack ({N}).
When you use a component that is not a weapon: Gain 1 stack.
Lasts the skirmish.

design.holes: The rage's value and the Nob's numbers are placeholders. Permanent for the fight, as built (Ryan, 4 November: "Nob permanent"; Claude's lean, since an elite's job is to make the player change plan). The rage is the foe's own from the start since 8 November: it was a Bellow, the Nob's opening move, so its first round fed nothing (Ryan: "It's not innate? ... That is so unbelievably incorrect").

table.stacks: Yes: the foe's rage a non-weapon spend
table.lasts: The fight; a Purge lowers the stacks, and the rage, the Nob's Ability, goes on

entries.name: Golden
entries.codex:
Attacks Gain:
  Hit: +2 damage dealt.
+1 Armour.
Gain Suppressed upon losing 25% Max HP since the start of the effect.
On Suppressed: Reduce stacks to 0.
Turn End: Reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: Monster Hunter's Rajang by archetype, Ryan's read of 4 November (the golden rage "is a mode, not an attack ... a cycle that forces the player into a cycle of attack and defense, broken by a bold player with great timing"). Claude's translation: the window is the decision, shield through its rounds or burst a quarter of its HP through the extra plate to stagger it; the lost action is the bold play's pay, where the swallow's release loses none (the stun row's care; the exit if it reads as a free stun). The add is the move's value and the plate a point; numbers placeholders.

table.stacks: Renews: a timer, one rage at a time
table.lasts: Laid as its turn ends, a stack going as each of its turns ends, ended early by a quarter of its HP lost or a Suppress

entries.name: Undying
entries.codex: When defeated: Consumed to return with full HP, acting from next round.

table.lasts: Until it falls; it returns once

entries.name: Aloft
entries.codex:
Cannot be targeted or hit. Other statuses still count down.
Removed when its gathered move lands.

design.holes: Ryan, 16 November: "I think the stoop can make it untargetable, yes. I don't think I'd call it phased though, it should still take damage from its riders, unlike phased. So it's different, should be a different buff, could be unique to the Roc for now if nothing else has that shape." And 17 November: "I'd say the roc doesn't get splashed while aloft." Content: aloft on a blow that gathers one round. Built on his second ruling as nothing new reaching it at all, with an aim or without, so equipment over every foe passes it by as a blast does and nothing breaks off a climb once it is up; what it carries is its own, a web and a Mine on it included. The name is a working one, his to change.

table.lasts: While its move gathers: from the turn it begins until the turn it lands or is broken off

entries.name: Appropriated
entries.codex:
Holds the stolen component's number: a weapon's damage, otherwise 1.
Consumed by the next Borrowed Blade, which deals this number.

design.holes: Ryan's mark of 15 November on the steal rider: "Doesn't need to be it's own rider. It grants Jammed on the target, and Gilgamesh gains Appropriated with the value. The ability should be renamed to Collect." Built 16 November as the first move written in steps: a blow that jams, then a step of its own (appropriate). His Ability, a count on his chip that follows what he holds (Ryan, the same day, of the purgeable buff a session had read from "gains": "I think Appropriated is a balance read. Maybe make it his ability, a number that fluctuates depending on what he's currently holding"). The swing is one strike at the piece's number, whatever strikes the piece had, and no keyword of the piece rides it. The steal rider and the foe's own field for what it held left the engine with it. The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: No: its number is the piece's, and what it takes next replaces it
table.lasts: Until its borrowed swing spends it

entries.name: Swallowed
entries.codex:
Cannot act. All ongoing effects are paused.
Immune to all damage. Cannot be targeted or hit by anything.
Round End: Reduce stacks by 1.
Reduce stacks to 0 upon {caster} losing 25% Max HP since the start of the effect.
Cannot be cleansed.

design.holes: Out of play, so everything it carries pauses (Ryan, 16 November: "Swallowed it's out of play so everything should pause"), where a Phased machine's ticks on: its Ablating, Scorched and Sapped wait, its Empowered and Brittle do not halve, its Regenerating pays nothing, it neither cools nor regenerates, a buff of its own holds nothing on the field (Essence Flare), and every timed status on it, a cooldown and a jam among them, moves a round later for each round's end it sits out: the rounds it sat out never came for it. Let go as its swallow's rounds run out, it is back before that round's end is read, the end it was owed from the round it was taken in; let go sooner, it goes on from where it stood. The swallow's own rounds run. It burns nothing while it is out and burns the turn it is back. A session's reads: an event of its fight still reaches it (a foe felled banks an Ammit's Essence), and a reboot it had begun before it was taken still recovers as the next round opens, the second half of a turn already given. Nothing cleanses it.

table.lasts: Laid as the round ends, a stack going as each round ends, ended early by its swallower falling or losing a quarter of its HP

entries.name: Guarded
entries.codex: Immune to all damage while every part stands.

table.lasts: While its parts stand

entries.name: Ability
entries.codex: A unit's own rule. Not a Buff or Debuff, so no Purge or Cleanse removes it.

design.holes: Ryan, 8 November, of the Nob's rage: "Nob, and any other enemies with a passive ability, should have an unpurgable passive chip that points out what's going on. Plus, that's how slay the Spire works, where he comes from. It's not a Buff, it's not a Debuff, it's labelled as an Ability, so it doesn't get purged. Can use this for player units as well, like the armadillo's form. Golden rage should be an ability chip too." The tile is a placeholder look, to judge on the phone (RIFTGATE_ABILITY_DEBUG=1).

entries.name: Barrier
entries.codex:
When Hit: Consumed to reduce damage to 0.
Turn Start: Removed.

table.lasts: A machine's until the next blow a foe lands on it, a foe's until a weapon's blow pops it; either until its next turn starts

entries.name: Ward
entries.codex:
Blocks every Debuff and Purge from the other side. Damage still applies.
Turn Start: Removed.

design.holes: A foe's move that lays a debuff without a blow is a rider too (Ryan, 25 October: "Should stop all riders, even from non-damaging attacks"), so a Stoke, a Stone, an Eruption on every machine and a Diamond Dust all pass a warded machine by. A foe's Ward (28 October) turns the team's marks (Effects.TEAM_MARKS), and since 2 November a stun and a Purge too, on either side, and stands (Ryan: nothing but damage lands on a Warded foe; the exception that let a stun through went with Numbed's roll).

table.lasts: Until its next turn starts

entries.name: Scorch
entries.codex: Resolve: Apply {N} Scorched per hit to each Frame hit.

entries.name: Menace
entries.codex: A pack's threat rating: a patrol 1 or 2, a formation 3, an elite or a boss 4. The Rupture meter, Anathema and salvage count it. Killing a pack pays its remaining Menace.

design.holes: One weight for the three tallies, flat by tier; salvage's growth by tier and what a boss pays are the economy pass's to set, the boss's four a placeholder.

entries.name: Elite
entries.codex: A unique Sprite leading its own pack, rated 4 Menace, arriving at a Fracture. It stands at the battle's tier.

design.holes: Placeholder kits in every domain for Ryan's marks; the Bone Wyvern waits on the slate.

entries.name: Seal
entries.codex: The boss cannot be attacked or join a skirmish until the Rupture breaks its seal.

design.holes: The seal's look on the ring is a first cut for the phone.

entries.name: Muster
entries.codex: Machine store, the Swallowtail's: a charge its Integrated components spend for their charged forms. Every die that rolls fills it a sliver, about thirty rolls a charge, and a kill by its own guns five rolls' worth; stored up to its cap. Starts each fight empty and never decays; a store, so no Purge touches it. With a charge up, its Integrated components go out charged unasked, unless the charged form has nowhere to land; then the plain form goes out and the charge waits.

design.holes: Every number is a placeholder; carrying it between fights is section 12's heat question.

table.stacks: Yes: a charge about thirty rolls of any die, five rolls' worth a kill by its guns, up to its cap
table.lasts: The skirmish; never decays

entries.name: Charged
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Shock.
  Resolve: Reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: The Shock primer (Ryan, 2 November), Primed's cousin, so Chain is the arcs alone and the Shock supply is a kit choice; a keyword on the weapon fired, never a mark per hit (3 November: "a multi-hit weapon with Shock would apply it after both hits"), so a strikes gun never cashes what it just laid. Its first granter is the Storm Petrel's lure in its Striker branch (17 November: "adds a self-grant of Charged stacks to the lure"), two stacks a spend.

table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Supercooled
entries.codex:
Weapons Gain:
  Cryo 1.
  Resolve: Reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: The Cryo primer (Ryan, 2 November: "laying 1 cryo at a time makes sense, keeps it a little unique, and avoids massive cooling spikes"; the name his pick), so any gun is a Cryo setter for a turn and the Cryo synergies open past the Cryo Flinger; a stack a strike after the hits (3 November: "resulting in 2 applications, not apply-cash-apply-cash, and not hit-hit-apply once"). No piece grants it yet.

table.lasts: Until spent

entries.name: Regenerating
entries.codex: Turn End: Gain 1 Shield per stack ({N}) on a Frame, or 1 HP per stack on a Sprite, then reduce stacks by 1.

design.holes: One clock on both sides since 15 November (Ryan: "These are structured as 'Regen 1 per stack' and I'd give all sources either a fixed duration, say 2 or 3 turns, or have it decay one stack at a time"; "Regenerating - agreed"), Ablating's turned round; a value at each of three turns until then. The machine half, built 30 October for the Storm Petrel's lock, which lays it no longer since its rework of 17 November, is kept with no piece granting it on Ryan's word of that day: "put machine regeneration back, that will literally be added in this session probably". Bought by whatever grants it, so a foe's purge takes it. The numbers are placeholders, the foes' unmoved by the new clock.

table.stacks: Yes: a point a stack, grants adding
table.lasts: A stack fades as each of its turns ends

entries.name: Ammo
entries.codex: The Musk Ox's magazine, a row of cells under its heat bar, a cell an ammo. Its weapons spend ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 2 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1, the price printed where the gun's heat would be; a foe's Scorched still heats them. The magazine holds 10, opens each fight at 3 and gains 1 at the start of every round after the first; a vent the Musk Ox spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2, an entry that is both 3, once. With too little left, a gun cannot be spent (DRY).

design.holes: Never a buff, so no Purge reaches it. If ammo runs plentiful, the vents' and shields' reloads or the trickle come down.

entries.name: Burrowed
entries.codex:
+1 Armour.
Fixed: Inertia Drill
Turn Start: Remove Broken, Overheated, Jammed and Corrupted. Gain 3 Shield and 5 Momentum, and lose 6 Heat.
Inertia Drill Gains:
  Resolve: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 16 November: "Instead of Reboot, it Burrows. While burrowed, it gains a unpurgable buff called 'Burrowed'"; an unpurgeable buff is labelled an Ability by his rule of 8 November. Its turns under his of 24 November: "When burrowed, it gains 50% shield regen, 50% cooling, and 50% Momentum generation", "50% of the final numbers, but represented as flat numbers"; "Burrow does not bank. But it does gain the 1 Armour." The text is a session's draft.

table.stacks: Renews: one, its armour the burrow's
table.lasts: Until it spends the Inertia Drill

entries.name: Momentum
entries.codex:
Maximum 10.
Gained by Burrowed and Applied Momentum.
Drained by Applied Momentum.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November: "Momentum is a Resource. It goes to 10 (subject to tuning)." Renamed from Conserved Momentum. The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until its drill drains it

entries.name: Applied Momentum
entries.codex:
Turn Start: Gain 1 Brittle and Pinned. Then, take a hit for 1 damage and drain 5 Momentum from the Mole. If 0 Momentum, removed and returned to the Mole.
Resolve: If hit, the Mole gains 1 Momentum.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November, his text: "Debuff, doesn't stack. Turn Start: Gain 1 Brittle and Pinned. Then, take 1 damage and drain 5 Momentum from the Mole. If 0 Momentum, remove and return to the Mole"; "The take 1 is a blow"; "Go to Resolve, and include area hits as well. Easily added to the Applied Momentum debuff: Resolve: The Mole gains 1 Momentum." His words, not yet signed on the Text tab.

table.lasts: Until its Mole's Momentum runs out, or the Mole burrows

entries.name: Frozen Momentum
entries.codex:
Turn Start: Gain 2 Brittle, 1 Cryo, Pinned, and Frozen. Then, take a hit for 1 damage and drain 5 Momentum from the Mole. If 0 Momentum, removed and returned to the Mole.
Resolve: If hit, the Mole gains 1 Momentum.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November, the Glacial Mole's: "Applied Momentum -> Frozen Momentum. Debuff, doesn't stack. Turn Start: Gain 2 Brittle, 1 Cryo, Pinned, and Frozen. Then, take 1 damage and drain 5 Momentum from the Mole. If 0 Momentum, remove and return to the Mole." Its Resolve line is Applied Momentum's, the form it takes the place of. His words, not yet signed on the Text tab.

table.lasts: Until its Mole's Momentum runs out, or the Mole burrows

Resolve: If hit, the Mole gains 1 Momentum.

Then, drain 5 Momentum from the Mole. If 0 Momentum, remove and return to the Mole." Its Resolve line is Applied Momentum's, the form it takes the place of. His words, not yet signed on the Text tab.

entries.name: Frozen
entries.codex: When Cryo would be consumed: Consumed to prevent it. Consume 1 Numbed, if any.

design.holes: Ryan, 24 November, the Glacial Mole's: "Frozen: Debuff. When any amount of Cryo would be consumed, consume 1 Numbed instead, if any, then remove Frozen"; "It gets the cooling. It is preserved regardless of numbed existing." His words, not yet signed on the Text tab.

table.lasts: Until a Cryo cash on it

entries.name: Drill Out
entries.codex:
Removed when Applied Momentum returns to the Mole.
On Burrowed: Removed.

design.holes: Ryan, 16 November: "It returns to the Mole when it burrows, taking the debuff with it"; 18 November, "Build the toggle". The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until its drill comes home: its Momentum runs out, or its next burrow

entries.name: Sonic Needle
entries.codex:
Gain 1 stack per hit from the Frame that laid it, and per hit this Sprite lands on that Frame.
Conducts Chain.
At 3 or more stacks: Chain 2 fires. Reduce stacks to 0.

design.holes: Ryan, 20 November: "Sonic Needle - Conducts Chain. On 3 stacks, the Echidna fires Chain 2, then consume all stacks on this foe"; his answers that day: the bolt is "targeted at nothing. So the foe that hit 3 stacks and procced it would take 2 by definition", and a stack a strike. Its branches tweak it: the Spiker's sap (1 less on the foe's attacks a stack) and Chaos's bolt leaving its foe one stack in place of none (Ryan, 21 November: "reduce stacks to 1"). The text is a session's draft.

table.lasts: Until a bolt consumes it
